look_here_first: Start with the red-oak leaf architecture: large deciduous leaves with 5–9 deep bristle-tipped lobes and conspicuous tufts of hair in the vein axils beneath. Then confirm with the shallow saucer-shaped acorn cup covering only about one-quarter to one-third of the nut.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower surface mostly glabrous except for conspicuous hair tufts in vein axils

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: terminal buds gray-brown and often noticeably 5-angled

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: acorns mature in the second year

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: acorn cup shallow saucer-shaped, covering about one-quarter to one-third of nut

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: FNA mature leaf blade usually 100–200 mm long; substantial overlap with other red oaks

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ripe saucer/cup often 7–12 mm deep and 15–30 mm wide, generally enclosing 1/4–1/3 nut

key_traits.label: Oak training
key_traits.text: Separate Shumard oak from Texas red oak by using the whole character set rather than leaf shape alone: Shumard generally has larger leaves, more mesic habitat, prominent vein-axil hair tufts beneath, and a broad shallow cup.
